clinicalPearls: A benign lipomatous tumour that classically occurs in the posterior neck, shoulder, and upper back of older men
It presents as a slow-growing, painless, well-defined subcutaneous mass in the characteristic cape or shawl distribution
Histology shows a mixture of mature adipocytes, bland CD34-positive spindle cells, and distinctive ropey collagen bundles, often with a myxoid matrix and mast cells
It shares loss of chromosome 13q material, including the RB1 locus, with pleomorphic lipoma and mammary-type myofibroblastoma, placing them on one molecular spectrum
Pleomorphic lipoma is a related lesion showing floret-type multinucleated giant cells
Strong CD34 positivity with retained bland cytology and loss of RB1 helps distinguish it from atypical lipomatous tumour
Unlike atypical lipomatous tumour and well-differentiated liposarcoma, it lacks MDM2 amplification
Marginal excision is curative and recurrence is uncommon
reference.pathophysiology: Spindle cell lipoma is a benign adipocytic neoplasm in which mature fat is replaced in varying proportion by bland spindle cells set within a matrix of characteristic thick, eosinophilic ropey collagen fibres, frequently accompanied by myxoid change and scattered mast cells. The tumour, together with its pleomorphic lipoma variant and mammary-type myofibroblastoma, is defined molecularly by deletions of the long arm of chromosome 13 that involve the RB1 tumour suppressor locus; loss of RB1 function drives the proliferation while permitting continued differentiation, so the cells remain cytologically banal. The spindle cells consistently express CD34. This molecular profile is fundamentally different from that of atypical lipomatous tumour and well-differentiated liposarcoma, which are characterised by amplification of MDM2 and CDK4, and the distinction is central to avoiding overtreatment of what is a wholly benign lesion.
additionalDifferentials: Atypical lipomatous tumour and well-differentiated liposarcoma
Myxoid liposarcoma when myxoid change is prominent
Nuchal-type fibroma or other collagen-rich lesions
additionalInvestigations: Ultrasound or MRI to characterise the subcutaneous fatty mass
Excisional or core biopsy with histological assessment
RB1 loss testing by immunohistochemistry or molecular methods in difficult cases
MDM2 amplification testing to exclude atypical lipomatous tumour when there is doubt
Correlation of site and cytology, as the classic distribution supports the diagnosis
redFlags: A deep or unusually large lesion, or one arising outside the classic distribution
Cytological atypia or lipoblasts raising concern for atypical lipomatous tumour or liposarcoma
Recurrence after excision prompting review of the original diagnosis
reference.prognosis: Spindle cell lipoma is benign with an excellent prognosis, and marginal excision is curative with recurrence being rare. The principal clinical value lies in confidently separating it from atypical lipomatous tumour to avoid unnecessarily aggressive management.
pitfalls: Misinterpreting the spindle cells or myxoid change as a liposarcoma
Overlooking the diagnosis when a lesion arises outside the classic neck and shoulder region
Confusing strong CD34 positivity with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans or solitary fibrous tumour
Failing to use MDM2 testing to exclude atypical lipomatous tumour in equivocal cases
references: WHO Classification of Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours
Enzinger and Weiss's Soft Tissue Tumors
management: Treat with marginal surgical excision, which is curative and rarely followed by recurrence
Confirm the benign diagnosis with histology and CD34-positive immunohistochemistry, correlating with the characteristic cape or shawl distribution
Distinguish from atypical lipomatous tumour and well-differentiated liposarcoma using RB1 loss and MDM2 amplification testing to avoid over-treatment
Offer conservative observation for small, asymptomatic lesions that are clinically and radiologically typical
Reassure regarding the excellent prognosis, with routine wound follow-up rather than intensive surveillance
Refer to a soft-tissue or sarcoma service when imaging or cytology raises doubt about a liposarcoma
